rationale: A2.3F requires solving systems of inequalities. Fidelity V2 uses the secure Systems Workspace construction mode so students must graph every boundary with the correct style and half-plane; the solution is the actual overlap, not a recognition answer.

documents.prompt: Solve the system by constructing both inequality graphs and shading ONLY their overlap: $y\ge {{m1}}x{{b1|signed}}$ and $y\le {{m2}}x{{b2|signed}}$.

solutionReview.headline: The system solution is the intersection of both half-planes.
reasoning: Both inequalities include equality, so both boundaries are solid.
Shade above the first boundary and below the second; keep only the common region.

attemptFeedback: A correct boundary is not enough; each line needs the correct style and the final shading must satisfy both inequalities.
supportHints: Graph one boundary and half-plane at a time, then keep only the overlap.

documents.prompt: Solve the system graphically: $y>{{m1}}x{{b1|signed}}$ and $y\le {{m2}}x{{b2|signed}}$. Construct the strict and inclusive boundaries correctly and shade only the overlap.

solutionReview.headline: Boundary style is part of the solution.
reasoning: The > inequality uses a dashed boundary and shades above.
The ≤ inequality uses a solid boundary and shades below.
Only their common region solves the system.

attemptFeedback: Check both the side you shaded and whether each boundary should be solid or dashed.
supportHints: Strict symbols > and < exclude the boundary; ≥ and ≤ include it.

variants.prompt: Solve the THREE-inequality system by constructing every boundary with the correct solid/dashed style and shading ONLY the common overlap: $y>{{m1}}x{{b1|signed}}$, $y\le{{m2}}x{{b2|signed}}$, and $y\ge{{c}}$.

solutionReview.headline: Three constraints increase construction load while the reasoning remains routine intersection work.
reasoning: Use a dashed first boundary, a solid second boundary, and a solid horizontal third boundary.
Keep only the region satisfying all three inequalities at once.

attemptFeedback: Check boundary style and shading direction for all three before identifying the overlap.
supportHints: A system means AND: every retained point must satisfy every inequality.

documents.prompt: Solve the THREE-inequality system. Construct every boundary and shade the region satisfying all three at once: $y\ge {{m1}}x{{b1|signed}}$, $y\le {{m2}}x{{b2|signed}}$, and $y>{{c}}$.

solutionReview.headline: “Two or more” means every half-plane must be satisfied simultaneously.
reasoning: Construct the first solid lower boundary and the second solid upper boundary.
The horizontal constraint y>{{c}} has a dashed boundary and shades above.
The final solution is the intersection of all three half-planes.

attemptFeedback: Do not stop after finding the overlap of two constraints; the third inequality can remove part of that region.
supportHints: For the horizontal boundary, use two points with y={{c}} and choose dashed because the inequality is strict.

documents.prompt: A planning model requires $y\ge x+{{upper}}$, $y\le x+{{lower}}$, and $y\ge {{floor}}$. Solve the THREE-inequality system by constructing every boundary and the common solution region.

context.title: Conflicting planning constraints
context.note: All three constraints must hold. If the first two correctly constructed half-planes have no overlap, adding a third constraint cannot create a solution.

solutionReview.headline: Contradictory parallel constraints make the whole three-inequality system infeasible.
reasoning: The first two boundaries have slope 1, so they are parallel.
The ≥ requirement is above the line with larger intercept {{upper}}, while the ≤ cap is below the line with smaller intercept {{lower}}.
Those two half-planes never overlap, so the additional floor $y\ge {{floor}}$ cannot restore a solution.

attemptFeedback: Do not invent an overlap. Correctly graphing contradictory constraints should leave no shared region.
supportHints: Check the two parallel constraints first. If they already contradict each other, the three-way intersection is empty.

documents.prompt: A student shades the UNION of the half-planes for $y>{{m1}}x{{b1|signed}}$, $y\le {{m2}}x{{b2|signed}}$, and $y\ge {{c}}$. Repair the error by constructing all three boundaries and showing ONLY the intersection that solves the system.

solutionReview.headline: A system uses logical AND, not union/OR.
reasoning: Each boundary must have its own correct solid/dashed style and half-plane.
The system solution keeps only points satisfying inequality 1 AND inequality 2 AND inequality 3.

attemptFeedback: The student's error is not fixed until your graph shows the common intersection of all three constraints.
supportHints: Construct all three half-planes, then keep only the region where all three shadings overlap.

variants.prompt: A student shades the UNION of the two half-planes $y>x-2$ and $y\le -x+4$. Diagnose the logical error and repair the graph by constructing both boundaries and shading ONLY their intersection.

solutionReview.headline: A system of inequalities uses logical AND, not OR.
reasoning: The first boundary is dashed and shades above; the second is solid and shades below.
Only the overlap satisfies both inequalities simultaneously.

attemptFeedback: The repair is complete only when the graph shows the common region, not both half-planes separately.
supportHints: Think intersection: points must satisfy inequality 1 AND inequality 2.
